title: Offline Tag Assignment Session Retirement
summary: retire unused browser-stored tag assignment staging and reconciliation so Series Tag Editor returns to one direct-save workflow
content_html:
Offline Tag Assignment Session Retirement

Result

Series Tag Editor has one persistence path: a direct, allowlisted Local Studio save to canonical tag assignments.

The browser-stored offline session, its Session and Import controls, exported session format, conflict reconciliation, and server preview/apply endpoints are removed. Series Tags remains the read-only cross-series coverage view and link to each Series Tag Editor.

Why

Offline staging was designed as failure recovery when direct local writes were less dependable. It was not adopted in practice and now adds a second save mode, browser-local state, conflict policy, import APIs, and UI that do not fit the repository's direct Studio workflow.

Keeping only direct save makes the persistence authority visible and avoids stranding changes in a browser profile or exported session file.

Boundary

  • Preserve canonical tag-assignments.json data and the current direct series/work assignment save contract.
  • When the local write service is unavailable or a save fails, keep the current unsaved editor state visible and report a contained failure; do not silently stage it elsewhere.
  • Remove offline storage, export, clear, import, preview/apply, conflict resolution, staged-row presentation, and their configuration and tests as one contract.
  • Do not add a replacement queue, sync layer, patch format, background retry, or compatibility reader.
  • Do not change tag scoring, inheritance, weights, alias-assisted selection, catalogue membership, or the read-only Series Tags table.
  • Bulk registry and alias imports are owned separately by Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement.

Feature Document

  • Offline Tag Assignment Session Removal Delivery — complete removal of the offline assignment contract.

Durable Destination

Shipped behavior belongs in Series Tag Editor, Series Tags, and Tag Services.

The feature is fully delivered. Canonical assignments and unrelated import systems remain independently owned.
